summary: The paper proposes a Toeplitz-matrix lens to categorize positional encodings as additive vs. multiplicative and empirically identifies a 'single-head deposit pattern' unique to RoPE on a position-sensitive synthetic task, supported by four ablations and a gradient-based theoretical argument. The mechanistic framing and the observed specialization phenomenon are interesting and the ablations are well-designed. However, the empirical validation is confined to a 6-layer Transformer on two synthetic tasks, the theoretical assumptions are strong and only loosely tied to the empirical findings, and the writing quality is uneven. The core claim that the deposit pattern is 'an intrinsic property of RoPE's multiplicative architecture' is not established on realistic language models, which is where such a claim ultimately matters.
strengths: The Toeplitz decomposition (Eqs. 1–2) is a clean, unifying description of additive vs. multiplicative PEs and gives a compact language to talk about content–position coupling.

The synthetic task pair (position-sensitive distance classification vs. position-agnostic counting) is well-designed to isolate the role of content–position coupling, and the qualitative predictions (RoPE strong on Task 1, penalized by inflexible bias on Task 2) are borne out.

The head-wise causal ablation making the 'deposit pattern' visible is compelling as a phenomenon within this setup, and the follow-up ablations (Absolute+RoPE, RoPE on a subset of heads, MLA hybrid, activation-level pi ablation) form a coherent chain of tests rather than one-off checks.

Attempting a formal gradient-flow argument (Props. 6.1–6.2, Thm. 6.1) for why the deposit pattern is intrinsic to RoPE — as opposed to only reporting the empirical artifact — is more ambitious than typical mechanistic-analysis papers.

key_concerns.issue: All empirical evidence is on a single 6-layer decoder trained on two hand-designed synthetic tasks. The paper repeatedly generalizes to 'RoPE's practical performance' and to real Transformer behavior, but never demonstrates that the deposit pattern (or any of the quantitative claims about generalization gaps) appears in a realistic language-modeling setting, in a ViT, or in any model of the scale where RoPE is actually deployed.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one non-toy setting — e.g., a small but real LM (WikiText-103 or a 100M-parameter causal LM) or an ImageNet-scale ViT — and repeat the head-ablation analysis to show whether a single-head deposit pattern (or a natural generalization of it) exists. Without this, the mechanistic claim about RoPE 'in general' is not supported.

key_concerns.issue: The theoretical section's link to the empirical phenomenon is weak. Assumptions A1–A3 are strong (bounded Jacobian singular values, existence of an 'anchor path' with a positive seed, a projection-separability condition specifically constructed to make ALiBi cancel) and are essentially engineered so that the desired asymmetry between RoPE and ALiBi holds. The 'exponential amplification' argument in Thm. 6.1 depends on gain factors γk>1 that are not shown empirically to hold in the trained models.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either (i) verify empirically that the quantities the theorem depends on (per-layer margins, γk factors, anchor-signal strength) behave as predicted during training, or (ii) tone down the theorem's language from 'the theoretical basis for the single-head deposit pattern' to a plausibility argument under idealized conditions.

key_concerns.issue: Novelty of the Toeplitz framing is overstated. Translation invariance = Toeplitz structure of the position-only Gram matrix is essentially a rewrite of the standard 'depends only on j−i' property of relative PE, and the additive/multiplicative dichotomy is already the way RoPE is usually contrasted with T5/ALiBi in the literature the paper cites. The decomposition xi = ci + pi is presented as a 'framework' but is essentially a book-keeping device.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Sharpen the contribution: clearly separate (a) analytical framing (modest novelty), (b) the empirical deposit-pattern observation (the paper's actual novel finding), and (c) the theoretical explanation. Rewrite the intro/contributions to avoid framing (a) as a primary contribution and instead lead with (b).

key_concerns.issue: Baselines and comparators are thin. The related-work section explicitly cites FoPE (Ermo et al., 2025), other RoPE variants, and the 'massive value'/rotation-artifact literature, but none of these appear as experimental comparators or targets of the analysis. The MLA experiment is a nice constructive comparison, but reporting a single MLA number in Table 1 with no seeds/CIs and no comparison to other hybrid designs is not enough to conclude MLA 'validates our theory'.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Include at least FoPE and one more recent RoPE variant on both synthetic tasks; report the head-ablation deposit-pattern signature for each, so the framework's predictions can be checked on more than one multiplicative scheme.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting is casual. 'Averaged over five seeds, and the variance is less than 5%' is stated once for all experiments, without figure-level CIs, error bars in the captions, or any test for whether the observed differences (e.g., the ~60% drop from ablating the deposit head vs. ~0% for others) are stable across seeds. Table 1 gives point estimates with no uncertainty.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add per-figure error bars/shaded bands and per-cell standard deviations in Table 1. For key claims (deposit head accuracy drop, RoPE vs. NoPE gap on Task 1) report a proper significance test or confidence interval across seeds.

key_concerns.issue: Writing quality is significantly below ICLR polish: many run-on sentences, awkward mid-sentence 'and this…', repeated content between adjacent paragraphs (e.g., framework description in Introduction and Methodology), and a scrambled ordering around Figure 1/Section 2. This impairs clarity in the theoretical section in particular.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: A careful copy-edit and reorganization — one clean statement of Assumptions 3.1/3.2 with justification, then Eqs. 1–2, and a single 'contributions' bulleted list — would substantially improve readability.

key_concerns.issue: The claim that Absolute+RoPE 'suppresses activation-level pi after Layer 2' (Ablation 4) is drawn from a caption-only figure and no quantitative gap between the pi-removal and random-vector-removal curves is given in the text.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report the numerical accuracy drops per layer for both interventions in a small table, so the reader does not have to trust that the two curves converge.

key_concerns.issue: The 'position-sensitive' task (predict binned relative distance between two unique trigger tokens over vocab 1000) is arguably tailor-made to reward RoPE's content–position coupling, since the only meaningful signal is the relative position of two anchors. This weakens the generality of 'RoPE decisively outperforms other methods'.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add one or two intermediate tasks (e.g., detect ordering of 3+ triggers, or a needle-in-haystack retrieval where distance matters but is not the answer) to show the effect is not specific to this exact objective.

questions_for_authors: Does the single-head deposit pattern appear in any non-synthetic setting (small LM, ViT)? If you have preliminary head-ablation numbers on a real model, please report them.
How sensitive is the deposit pattern to model depth and head count? Does it persist in a 12- or 24-layer model, or is it partly a small-model phenomenon?

In Ablation 2 (only 1–2 RoPE-enabled heads), what happens on Task 2 in the same configuration? Task 1 numbers alone cannot distinguish 'sufficient specialization' from 'RoPE routes everything through one head regardless'.

Can Assumption A3 (projection separability) be empirically checked in the trained ALiBi model, and does Proposition 6.2's cancellation predict the ALiBi Task-1 failure quantitatively (not just qualitatively)?
For the MLA result in Table 1: are 88.34/97.41 averages over seeds, and what are the standard deviations? Also, is MLA tuned comparably to RoPE (parameter count, learning rate)?

How does the framework treat learned relative-bias schemes like FoPE and the frequency-partitioned variants cited in Related Work? Do they fall under the additive Toeplitz category, and if so, do they exhibit any deposit-like pattern?
calibration_check: Claims about the synthetic-task behavior are appropriately scoped, but statements that the deposit pattern is 'an intrinsic property of RoPE's multiplicative architecture' and that this explains 'the gap between RoPE's theoretical promise and its practical performance' overreach what a 6-layer model on two synthetic tasks can support; the limitations section partially acknowledges this but the main text does not.

significance.justification: The deposit-pattern observation is a genuinely interesting mechanistic finding, but confined to a toy setting it is unlikely to change practice or drive follow-up work at the scale ICLR readers care about.

novelty.justification: Toeplitz/translation-invariance framing is largely a re-encoding of well-known facts; the novel contribution is really the empirical deposit-pattern observation plus the gradient-flow argument, which is modest but not incremental.

rigor.justification: Ablations are causal and well-structured within the synthetic setting, but the theoretical assumptions are strong and engineered, and the empirical–theoretical link is loose.

statistical_soundness.justification: Seeds and rough variance are mentioned but no per-figure error bars, no significance tests, and Table 1 reports point estimates with no uncertainty for a key claim.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations section correctly flags the length-extrapolation gap and task complexity, but main-text claims about RoPE 'in general' and about the theory 'explaining' the deposit pattern are stronger than the evidence warrants.

clarity.justification: Numerous run-on sentences, repeated content between intro and method, and a jumbled Figure 1 area make the paper harder to read than a typical ICLR submission.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard sections are present and within a reasonable length; the ablation section is well-organized around hypotheses.

reproducibility.justification: Synthetic tasks are described in enough detail to be reconstructed and the model architecture is small and specified, but many quantitative details are deferred to appendices and some claims (e.g., MLA setup, hybrid PE) are described only sketchily in the body.

related_work.justification: Covers the main PE families and cites the relevant mechanistic-analysis literature, but does not experimentally compare to any of the recent RoPE variants (FoPE, etc.) that would be the natural comparators.

figure_quality.justification: Figures/captions clearly support their specific claims (learning curves, violin plots of ablation drops, layer-wise pi-removal), though several depend on visual pattern-reading that would benefit from accompanying tables of numbers.

breadth_generality.justification: One 6-layer decoder, two synthetic tasks, no real-language or vision validation — the generality implied by phrases like 'RoPE's practical performance' is not supported by the experimental scope.

overall_recommendation.justification: Interesting mechanistic observation and a reasonable analytical lens, but the narrow experimental scope, over-strong theoretical framing, and thin statistical reporting put this below the ICLR acceptance bar in its current form.
